name: K3s
what_it_is: K3s is a fully conformant, production-ready Kubernetes distribution packaged as a single binary under 100 MB, targeting edge, IoT, CI/CD, ARM, and embedded environments. It halves the memory footprint of upstream Kubernetes by consolidating components, removing in-tree cloud/storage drivers, and defaulting to SQLite instead of etcd.
protocols: WebSocket tunneling (kubelet API between worker and control plane)
configuration: K3S_TOKEN environment variable (required for cluster join)
K3S_URL environment variable (agent points to server at https://server:6443)
Datastore backend selectable: SQLite3 (default), etcd3, MariaDB, MySQL, PostgreSQL
Auto-deployment of Kubernetes resources from local manifest directory
Bundled components (Flannel, Traefik, CoreDNS, etc.) can be disabled or swapped
modes: Server mode: sudo k3s server (runs control plane + agent)
Agent mode: sudo k3s agent --server https://[server]:6443 --token [token] (worker only)
constraints: Requires privileged mode when running in containers (e.g., docker-compose)
tmpfs required for /run and /var/run when containerized
In-tree cloud provider drivers removed — must use out-of-tree CCM alternatives
In-tree storage drivers removed — must use CSI out-of-tree alternatives
Single binary architecture couples all control-plane components into one process
K3S_TOKEN must be shared out-of-band between server and agent nodes
docker_services: server (rancher/k3s, ports 6443/80/443, persistent volume k3s-server, privileged)
agent (rancher/k3s, persistent volume k3s-agent, privileged, restart: always)
notable_absences: No built-in fault injection or chaos engineering support
No detailed scaling or cluster-size limits documented
No native distributed tracing or log aggregation component
No out-of-the-box network encryption between nodes (no WireGuard by default)
No multi-tenancy or namespace isolation enforcement beyond upstream Kubernetes RBAC
